{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693912034,"sessionID":"ses_e23e9ef93ffeMyXvuuCXse8GWE","part":{"id":"prt_1dc17d56f001hcmv9GDtw5lXBV","messageID":"msg_1dc17b565001CtR99w2GOcqBje","sessionID":"ses_e23e9ef93ffeMyXvuuCXse8GWE","type":"text","text":"I found and fixed four problems. All four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from about minute 77 until the shift ended at minute 120.\n\n1. **stock-svc, bad deploy v25** (started at minute −14): the build cut the cache expiry to 1/600th of its setting. stock-svc got overloaded and started failing; that took web-storefront to about 95% errors and admin-portal to about 28%. I rolled it back and it was done by minute 18.\n2. **payouts-svc, stuck overload**: it was getting about three times its normal traffic and was caught in a retry storm, failing 87% of requests. stock-svc depends on it, so web-storefront kept failing after the rollback. I couldn't find what caused the extra traffic; the one recent deploy on a payouts-svc caller (returns-svc) looked harmless. I rejected 80% of payouts-svc's requests up front to break the retry loop. Then I scaled it from 6 to 16 replicas and lifted that limit at minute 55, and it recovered.\n3. **media-svc, bad deploy v98** (minute −26): it made request deadlines 10 times shorter, so callers saw timeouts. mobile-api ($12,400/min) and partner-api were losing 4% of requests through it. I added replicas before rolling it back so the rollback wouldn't overload it. After that I set it back to its normal 6 replicas, which costs nothing.\n4. **emails-svc, bad config cfg-58** (started at minute 61, during the shift): it removed the `orders.write` permission, and web-storefront went to 51% errors. I reverted it at minute 76. There was also a deploy (v176) at the same minute that I never checked; errors went to zero after the config revert, so I left it alone.\n\n**Remaining cost:** payouts-svc stays at 16 replicas, which costs $30/min in extra replicas from minute 52 to the end of the shift. I didn't set it back to 6 because its traffic was still about three times normal and rising slowly. At 6 replicas it would very likely have overloaded again. At 16 it was running at about 81% CPU and on track to reach about 89% by minute 120.\n\nI didn't apply any mitigation to a service that turned out not to need it.","time":{"start":1794693911919,"end":1794693912031}}}
